questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me to study at a university that offers relevant and exciting subjects in relation to my studies. Furthermore, it was also important for me to study in a city that I feel like living in and exploring.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My experience has been amazing. Both academically and socially, I have spoken the Turkish language, read a lot of Turkish texts, explored the city, and made new acquaintances. I am happy!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy, the university was really good at guiding Erasmus students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was in constant contact with the university through mail, when we arrived meetings were held where all the important information was told.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: My family found it through the internet, there are a lot of apartments in Istanbul in all price ranges. It's not a problem.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Bogazici University is a university where you spend a lot of time on campus until late at night, where there are a lot of students in addition, there are also a lot of bars and restaurants around the school. It has therefore not been a problem for me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was easy KU and BU guided me a lot!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was supposed to start at Hacettepe universitesi in Ankara, but I have always wanted to study in Istanbul at Bogazici and therefore sought to bypass the original process. It was actually not much different than what the other students were going through. It was actually the same process, but the difference was that my process started a lot earlier.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was help from KU and BU all the time if I had some questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got accepted to all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Never hesitate to ask questions and always check your email.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was sufficiently difficult. However, there were two courses that really challenged me, but despite that, I made it through all of the courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We often had to write discussion papers, which are reminiscent of the written exams at KU. In addition, the teaching in the classes is also reminiscent of each other, where there is a dialogue between teacher and students, the main difference was that there was more group work at BU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Fagelementkode: TKF 217.01: Intermediate reading in Turkish ( ECTS 6)

Fagelementkode: TKL 309.01: Turkish poetry in the republican period ( ECTS 4)
Fagelementkode: TKL 433.01: Short story in modern Turkish literature (ECTS 5)
Fagelementkode: TKL 211.01: Modernization in Turkish literature ( ECTS 6)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't encounter any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Because of the country's inflation, the prices were higher than normal.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is an inside and outside pool for students, a gym and halls.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of different clubs that you can be a member of such as book clubs, art clubs, music, sports clubs, and many more. Further more there are a lot of parties and concerts at the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them! Especially to be a member at one of the clubs because there is a club for every interest almost.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Istanbul is an incredible city and the rest of Turkey as well therefore would I recommend you to just explore!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy also because I was together with students from other foreign countries and we explored the country and culture together. But it is important to be open to new experiences!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk with them!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate the fact that Turkish people are open and talkative, and the vibrant and dynamic culture in the city. I am in love with Istanbul! The city by itself is enough for me.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Talk with students!
Explore the most amazing city Istanbul!
Remember to enjoy every moment because the time pass so fast!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The whole experience actually!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: In the beginning, I was feeling lonely in the big city, I didn't know anyone, but trust me it will change!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
